name: Nori Robotics

business_model.summary: Nori Robotics builds and sells a low-cost bimanual mobile robot for $1,688, targeted at robotics developers and researchers, with optional paid software.

evidence.quote: We make money by selling the hardware for $1,688, with optional paid software on top.

team.summary: The company was founded by Antonio, who has a background in robotics research at Columbia University.

evidence.quote: I’m Antonio from Nori Robotics
I started working on Nori while doing robotics research at Columbia.

product.summary: Nori A3 is a $1,688 bimanual mobile robot with 19 degrees of freedom, two arms, a wheeled base, four cameras, and a Raspberry Pi 5.

evidence.quote: We build a $1,688 bimanual mobile robot in San Francisco for robotics developers and researchers.
After seven iterations the latest Nori has: * 19 degrees of freedom * Two 7+1 DOF arms with a 1.5 kg payload per arm

competitors.summary: The company faces competition from low-cost Chinese robots, K-scale labs, and Unitree.

evidence.quote: sad to see it shut down due to the competition with low-cost chinese robots
evidence.author: TristanX

evidence.quote: Have you chatted with the ex developers of KScale labs? What makes you different, given they went poof?
evidence.author: OsrsNeedsf2P

evidence.quote: when the Unitree G1 or whatever falls over the result is catastrophic.
evidence.author: arjie

why_now.summary: There is a strong need for affordable hardware in robotics research to enable large dataset collection and testing, which was previously limited by expensive robots.

evidence.quote: getting my hands on affordable hardware was difficult. Most labs have one or two expensive robots
Low-cost humanoids finally make those quirky home automation dev projects affordable.
evidence.author: Mugshelf

risks.risk: Intense competition from low-cost Chinese robots and the challenge of building a sustainable business in a hardware race to the bottom.

evidence.quote: sad to see it shut down due to the competition with low-cost chinese robots
evidence.author: TristanX

evidence.quote: making a sustainable business on a hardware race to the bottom sounds challenging.
evidence.author: mNovak

risks.risk: Technical limitations of cheap components, such as jerky RC servos and an underpowered Raspberry Pi 5.

evidence.quote: The biggest problem is they are using RC style servos. This is why all the arm motions are jerky and lack precision.
evidence.author: elictronic

evidence.quote: RPi5 seems a bit underpowered for all the sensors & control and offloading to a computer through wifi seems problematic.
evidence.author: slug

risks.risk: Skepticism regarding the truthfulness of the robot's advertised capabilities and video demonstrations.

evidence.quote: So I guess my main question is: What do you hope to accomplish by shamelessly lying?
evidence.author: Mawr

evidence.quote: Are these videos of it eg tidying up real or just staged / cherry picked?
evidence.author: jonplackett

founder_depth.why: Antonio has a technical background doing robotics research at Columbia and has iterated on the hardware, but there is no evidence of prior exits or commercial shipping experience.

shipping_evidence.why: The company has shipped its first robot, published a hardware paper on arXiv, and released an open SDK on GitHub alongside a browser-based simulator.

evidence.quote: We’ve shipped our first robot and are building the next batch.
Our open SDK includes teleoperation and demonstration tools: https://github.com/Nori-Robotics/nori-sdk-py
More details are in our hardware paper: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2605.16537

demand_signal.why: There is strong interest and engagement on Hacker News regarding the low price point, but no named enterprise customers or revenue figures are provided.

evidence.quote: That price point is really tempting.
evidence.author: Tepix

evidence.quote: 2k is the price point for me where I might buy a big thing every so many years
evidence.author: mrnotcrazy

defensibility.why: The hardware relies on cheap off-the-shelf components like RC servos and is partially open-source, making it highly vulnerable to copycats and low-cost Chinese competitors.

evidence.quote: Some main choices we made to get the cost low was using high-ratio servos instead of QDD motors
Parts of hardware are open source.
sad to see it shut down due to the competition with low-cost chinese robots
evidence.author: TristanX

analysis.case_summary: The strongest point is the highly disruptive $1,688 price point that democratizes robotics development, while the weakest point is the severe technical limitation of using cheap RC servos and a Raspberry Pi 5, which may prevent the robot from performing precise real-world tasks.
would_change_my_mind: Evidence of significant pre-orders or recurring software revenue from the optional paid software tier.
Demonstration of precise, non-jerky autonomous task execution in unstructured real-world environments without teleoperation.
Partnerships with major research labs or universities adopting Nori as their standard development platform.
data_gaps: No information on the pricing or features of the optional paid software.
No details on the exact number of pre-orders or revenue generated so far.
No information on the background or size of the rest of the founding team besides Antonio.
